purpose: Every defect this repository has ever found -- in its tools, in its examples, or in its own documentation -- gets one record. The record is closed only when it answers four questions mechanically: (1) what shape was the defect (class), (2) why did our checking miss it (escape_cause), (3) what root cause was changed, (4) what gate now kills this class and how that gate was shown to fire. A defect recorded as prose cannot be interrogated; a defect recorded here can be, by tools/defect-closure.py.

escape_cause_taxonomy.E1: no gate existed at the time the defect was made
escape_cause_taxonomy.E2: a gate existed but did not cover this shape (substring for structure, first column for the table, a sample set that never contained the case)
escape_cause_taxonomy.E3: a gate fired but had no landing -- printed, noted, logged, and never entered the exit code
escape_cause_taxonomy.E4: a gate existed but had never been shown capable of failing -- a decorative gate; it was believed to be running and it was not discriminating

class_taxonomy: docs/taxonomy.md -- SF-001 .. SF-014 across five families (A Vacuous Verification, B Uncounted Absence, C Wrong Evidence, D Drifting Oracle, E Process & Environment)

entries.symptom: A handler that correctly recorded a failure was reported as a silent one: _silent_body_kinds() accumulated silent statement kinds and returned them if non-empty, never verifying that EVERY statement was silent.
entries.found_by: running the linter on its own source (building-this-catalog #1)
entries.root_cause: the rule tested a property of SOME statements while claiming a property of ALL of them; the sample pair only ever contained all-silent bodies, so the quantifier was never exercised
entries.gate_added: gate-lint.py sample pair extended to a mixed body; the rule returns [] as soon as any statement is not a discard
entries.evidence: the mixed 'record then continue' handler is no longer flagged -- the finding that produced this entry is gone

entries.symptom: SFL-005 decided whether a test runner's output was guarded by searching the raw text for the word 'collected'; the bad sample's docstring contained that word, so the rule concluded a guard existed and stayed silent.
entries.found_by: --selftest: the bad sample was not flagged (building-this-catalog #2)
entries.root_cause: identifier (a guard construct) was detected by substring instead of by structure; the sample's surrounding prose leaked into the detection
entries.gate_added: SFL-005 detects a guard construct via the AST (Compare over a string literal, or a pattern-match call), not a mention in prose
entries.evidence: the bad sample is now flagged by --selftest

entries.symptom: check-catalog.py asserted each entry id appeared in the index files with 'if eid in text'; after a link was deliberately mangled to SF-014-REMOVED the assertion still passed, because 'SF-014' occurs inside the mangled string.
entries.found_by: reverse control A: mangle a link, assert a non-zero exit (building-this-catalog #3)
entries.root_cause: the validator had no negative control that mangled a link, so it had never been observed failing on the exact shape it existed to catch
entries.gate_added: check-catalog.py asserts the entry FILENAME is linked, not that its id occurs as text; reverse control A is part of the suite
entries.evidence: mangling a link now forces a non-zero exit

entries.symptom: gate-lint.py /nonexistent/path.py printed 'no Python files found' and exited 0 -- being asked to check something that does not exist and reporting success.
entries.root_cause: an empty target set was treated as a pass; the gate had never been run against a target that does not exist
entries.gate_added: explicit targets that do not exist are a failure; so is 'nothing was linted'
entries.evidence: gate-lint on a missing path now exits non-zero

entries.symptom: Tree-level findings (SFL-006) were printed but never added to the severity counters; the visible output contained a finding while --strict exited 0.
entries.found_by: reverse control C run in strict mode (building-this-catalog #5)
entries.root_cause: the finding had no landing: it was reported into a channel that did not feed the exit code, and nothing required a reported finding to move it
entries.gate_added: tree-level findings enter the same counters as file-level ones; reverse control C
entries.evidence: --strict with a tree-level finding now exits non-zero

entries.symptom: '# gate-lint: ignore SFL-001' was matched with a plain regex over the source; gate-lint.py's own docstring quotes that directive, so the file suppressed SFL-001 for itself.
entries.found_by: reading the inline-suppressions note in the linter's own output (building-this-catalog #6)
entries.root_cause: the suppression directive was matched anywhere in the text rather than only inside a comment token
entries.gate_added: the directive is honoured only inside a tokenize.COMMENT token; if the source cannot be tokenised, suppressions are ignored (fail toward 'checked')
entries.evidence: gate-lint.py no longer suppresses SFL-001 for itself

entries.symptom: Unreadable files were announced on stdout and then dropped; the run could still exit 0. An unlinted file is an unverified file.
entries.found_by: reading the SFL-002 finding on the linter's own source (building-this-catalog #7)
entries.root_cause: the problem had a representation (a printed line) but no landing: no path carried it into the exit code, so an unlinted file looked like a clean run
entries.gate_added: unreadable files are counted, listed, and force a non-zero exit
entries.evidence: an unreadable input now forces a non-zero exit

entries.symptom: SFL-003 was released at severity 'medium'; measured against two files of ordinary tooling it produced four findings and zero true positives, while still affecting the exit code.
entries.found_by: running the linter on its own source and reading every finding (building-this-catalog #8)
entries.root_cause: a rule's stated confidence was not the measured one; nothing required a rule to be run against ordinary code and its precision read before release
entries.gate_added: sample-pair requirement + a rule must declare its MEASURED confidence and known false positives; SFL-003 demoted to low/confidence-low, scoped to module level
entries.evidence: SFL-003 now carries its measured precision in its own false-positives note

entries.symptom: make-manifest.py rebound 'digest' inside a loop and returned the hash of the last file instead of the set digest; the file written to disk was correct, the printed/returned value was wrong, and the tool's own verifier then rejected the tool's own output.
entries.found_by: --check disagreeing with the generator's own stdout (building-this-catalog #9)
entries.root_cause: no gate required a reported value to be produced by a second, independent route; one expression both wrote the artifact and supplied the return value
entries.gate_added: generate / --check / --print-digest must all yield one identical value (three independent channels)
entries.evidence: the three channels agree after the loop variable was renamed to file_digest

entries.symptom: A comment claimed the '(?:\.git)?' token was load-bearing and that selftest case 3 had caught a false positive from its absence; re-running case 3 against the 'broken' regex showed it passes under both, so the claim described a defect that never existed.
entries.found_by: testing a comment instead of trusting it (building-this-catalog #10)
entries.root_cause: the claim was produced by reasoning, not by running; selftest case 3 could not distinguish the two regexes, so the suite had no power over the claim
entries.gate_added: AGENTS rule 10 (do not assert a necessity you have not measured) + the claim was replaced by the measured result, with the measurement kept
entries.evidence: case 3 passes under both regexes -- the original claim is now recorded as measured-false

entries.symptom: Five statements across three files claimed CI ran the gates and enforced the manifest; .github/workflows/ did not exist. The repository whose subject is 'a check believed to be running, and not running' had a CI believed to be running and not running.
entries.root_cause: no gate existed that checked whether a workflow the documentation asserted actually exists; an absent run emits nothing and looked identical to a run that passed
entries.gate_added: .github/workflows/gates.yml added and the README badge repointed at the real run
entries.evidence: the workflow's first execution failed a gate that a local run had reported passing

entries.symptom: check_readme_agreement() compared only the FIRST column of the S5 crosswalk table; a change in the semantic mapping columns (the exact Q4/D1 drift the previous correction was about) stayed green.
entries.found_by: ITU FG-TIDA round-3 review (use-cases#21, comment 6033701828, 2026-10-07T08:04Z), confirmed by our own gate 9 on first run
entries.root_cause: the mutation suite M1-M4 all targeted the artifact under test (implementation.py); not one mutation was aimed at a checker, so the gate's own blind spot (first column standing in for the whole table) was never exercised by anything we ran
entries.gate_added: gate 9 (tools/checker-mutation.py) + _readme_agreement_negative_controls(); the agreement gate now compares every normalised column
entries.evidence: tampering crosswalk column 2 or column 3 now turns the selftest red; restoring returns it to green

entries.symptom: The act-window branch still pre-classified the temporal answer: it injected freeze_state = FREEZE_POST_VERDICT directly, and the binding-token structure changed with it, so Q6's own inference ('the binding was lost when the freeze landed after the verdict') was handed to it rather than derived.
entries.root_cause: the contract supplied, as input, the very conclusion the check was supposed to reach -- a tautology oracle; and nothing proved the branch could still reach the conclusion once the label was removed
entries.gate_added: act-window now carries ordinary observations only (check time, actuation time, freeze-effective time, binding/source/generation); Q6 derives the binding loss itself
entries.evidence: harness selftest green with freeze_state absent from the observation set

entries.symptom: exit_code was produced before _apply_mutant() changed the final verdict, and the kill matrix then took observed[1:], discarding that first field -- leaving internally contradictory observations such as FAIL + EXECUTE + APPLY + target changed.
entries.root_cause: no assertion crossed exit status against guard decision, attempted action and target state; the observation contract had never been shown to reject a contradictory record
entries.gate_added: exit status is recomputed from the final verdict, and _assert_observation_coherence() asserts agreement across the four fields
entries.evidence: a deliberately contradictory observation record now raises in the selftest

entries.symptom: The harness said mutations were applied after the runner had ruled, but M2-cache-read changed the input BEFORE the decision, and M1-M4 inject behavioural deviation around the implementation rather than mutating implementation.py; the description and the code described different layers.
entries.root_cause: the README's mutant table had no 'class' column, so nothing connected the described layer to the implemented layer, and no gate parsed the description
entries.gate_added: the README mutant table gained a class column and check_readme_agreement() now validates it; gate 9 carries a MUTCLASS mutation against that column
entries.evidence: tampering the mutant class column now turns the selftest red

entries.symptom: On its first run, gate 9 found that 7 of the S5 selftest's 12 decision points had never been shown capable of failing: row-count truncation, target-vs-action, blinding, self-report ban, spec fields, row-4 trace, and surviving-mutant reporting all passed unconditionally.
entries.root_cause: the mutation suite guarded the artifact, not the guards; nothing in the repository asked of a check the question it asks of everyone else -- can it fail?
entries.gate_added: gate 9 with 7 new negative controls; every check now has a mutation that must be killed
entries.evidence: before: S9 FAILED, 7 findings; after: 12 checks killed, 7 controls load-bearing, 2 sentinels green

entries.symptom: AGENTS.md and index.md both described the gate list as 'seven gates' while .githooks/pre-commit ran nine; the count had drifted twice (8, then 9) with no gate noticing, because the number is restated as a literal in prose instead of read from the hook.
entries.found_by: this round, while adding rule 13/14 to AGENTS.md
entries.root_cause: the gate count had no single source of truth: it was asserted as a literal in several documents, and no gate compared those literals against the hook that actually defines the list
entries.gate_added: a gate-count consistency check in verify_release_consistency.py (any 'Runs all N gates' / 'the same N gates' literal in a living document must equal the hook's real count; CHANGELOG.md is excluded as a historical record) + the documents now point at the hook instead of restating a number
entries.evidence: with the check in place, restoring the literal 'seven gates' into AGENTS.md makes gate 6 fail, and restoring the hook-derived wording returns it to green -- the drift D-017 describes is now mechanically rejected

entries.symptom: gate-lint.py crashed with a bare KeyError: 'PARSE' when pointed at a file containing a syntax error: lint_source() emitted Finding('PARSE', ...) but RULES never registered 'PARSE', so every RULES[f.rid]['severity'] lookup raised instead of reporting the unparseable file.
entries.found_by: this round, running gate-lint against a tool that had a syntax error (defect-closure.py, mid-edit)
entries.root_cause: a finding's rule id was never required to resolve in RULES; nothing had ever fed gate-lint an unparseable file, so the crash path had no negative control and had never been shown to run
entries.gate_added: RULES['PARSE'] is now registered, and gate-lint --selftest feeds an unparseable source and asserts the PARSE finding appears with an id that resolves
entries.evidence: gate-lint --selftest now fires PARSE on an unparseable sample without crashing

entries.symptom: Entry D-017 was recorded as closed with a gate_added describing 'a gate-count consistency check in verify_release_consistency.py', but that check was not yet in the tree -- the ledger asserted a gate that did not exist, and gate 10 accepted the entry because it only validated that the field was a non-empty string.
entries.found_by: this round, cross-checking the ledger against the tree before adding more entries
entries.root_cause: gate 10 validated the SHAPE of gate_added but never its referent; a free-text claim of a gate is indistinguishable from a real one, so a premature closure passed. The ledger was acting as authority for a check that was not there.
entries.gate_added: defect-closure.py now extracts every path-like token from gate_added and requires it to resolve to an existing file, and any tools/*.py it names to be invoked by .githooks/pre-commit; two negative controls cover both branches (a missing gate, an unwired tool). Residual gap, stated rather than hidden: it can prove a named gate EXISTS and runs, not that the check inside it is the one described -- that stays a review-time judgement.
entries.evidence: the two new negative controls are caught by --selftest ('does not exist' and 'no gate hook invokes'), and the real ledger passes once D-017's check is actually present in verify_release_consistency.py
